newsitem.title: JAPAN: Taiwan's Mosel plans samurai issue - Nikko.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Mosel plans samurai issue - Nikko.

text.p: Taiwan chipmaker Mosel Vitelic Inc is planning to issue about 12-15 billion yen worth of samurai bonds around the middle of June, an underwriter at Nikko Securities Co Ltd, which has been appointed lead-manager of the issue, said on Monday.
"Mosel is considering launching samurai bonds with a duration of about five years," the underwriter said.
Taiwanese firms have raised funds in the Euro market in the past, but this will be the first time a private firm has offered yen-denominated bonds publicly, the underwriter said.
Many overseas borrowers are keen to raise funds through yen-denominated bonds as they can take advantage of lower Japanese interest rates.
"It (Mosel Vitelic) can also make its name in the market by issuing samurais," the underwriter said. "We are hoping that many Taiwanese firms will follow this move."
